cards.explanation: The answer is the Pharisees and all the Jews. Mark says that in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially (Mark 7:3). The Pharisees are the strict religious leaders, and the writer says it's all the Jews, so this was a whole-community tradition. That's a lot of people washing before a meal.

The answer is False. Mark says that on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash (Mark 7:4). So a trip to the market means a washing before the meal. I walk past a mixing bowl and just start stamping, so this level of routine impresses me.

The answer is that they want to know why the disciples skip the elders' tradition. They ask, "Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders?" (Mark 7:5). They add that the disciples eat with defiled hands. Unwashed hands, friends. UNWASHED. HANDS.

The answer is True. In the words Jesus quotes, "These people honor Me with their lips…" (Mark 7:6). It's the very next part that stings, because the quote goes on to say "…but their hearts are far from Me." (Mark 7:6). Honoring God with the lips while the heart is far from Him is exactly what Jesus is naming.

The answer is the precepts of men. The quote says, "They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men." (Mark 7:7). Precepts are rules, and these are rules that came from men. Jesus is pointing at the difference between what God said and what people added.

The answer is commandment. Jesus says, "You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men." (Mark 7:8). Two things are on the table, God's commandment and a tradition of men. Jesus says they dropped the first to hold the second.

The answer is nothing at all anymore. Jesus says that once a man says it's Corban, he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother (Mark 7:12). Not a little, not a bit. Nothing. That's how a tradition could undo "Honor your father and your mother…" (Mark 7:10).

The answer is anything that enters him from outside. Jesus says, "Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him…" (Mark 7:15). That turns the whole handwashing argument on its head. The thing that counts isn't what goes in.

The answer is True! Jesus says, "but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him." (Mark 7:15). Everybody had been arguing about what goes IN, all that hands and washing talk. Then Jesus turns it around to what comes OUT, and I bet that crowd got quiet fast. It's like scrubbing the outside of a mixing bowl until it sparkles while nobody asks what's in the dough.

The answer is False. Jesus tells the disciples that what enters a man from the outside "…does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated." (Mark 7:19). The stomach gets it, and the heart doesn't. That's why the outside stuff can't defile a man the way what comes from within does.
The answer is clean. Mark adds, "(Thus all foods are clean.)" (Mark 7:19). It's the writer's own note after Jesus' words. Where I come from, that's good news for every cookie too.

The answer is from within the hearts of men. Jesus says, "For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts…" (Mark 7:21). The trouble comes from the heart, not from the plate. That's why scrubbing hands can't fix it.
